key_insight: Eliminating redundant plateau operators in ADAPT-VQE, especially with pool restoration, makes optimization faster and shallower, while OBDF downfolding improves active-space energies toward FCI.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to cut quantum circuit depth and iterations in near-term quantum chemistry workflows without changing the underlying ADAPT-VQE framework.
method: Detect and remove non-contributing operators once optimization plateaus are identified.
Compare ADAPT-VQE variants with and without pool restoration after elimination.
Combine ADAPT-VQE with OBDF to replace the bare active-space Hamiltonian by a correlated effective Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on linear H6 chain, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2 with OpenFermion show reduced circuit depth and iteration count, and OBDF-ADAPT-VQE energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE in the same active space.
watch_item: Operator elimination and downfolding gains depend on reliable plateau detection and the quality of the effective Hamiltonian, so performance may be system- and threshold-sensitive.
paper_title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
